quarterly_data.quarter: Lam Research Citi’s Global TMT Conference 2026 (09-09-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: FIRST READ ON 2028: the CY2026 WFE walk ('from $135 billion to $140 billion, now to low $150 billion'), the clean-room constraint and the '8 to 10 new, what I would call tier 1 fabs coming online ... through the end of 2027' were all reaffirmations of the Q4 FY2026 call. NEW here is the year beyond: CFO Doug Bettinger would not commit to a 2028 number, but said that because customers are telling him 2027 is still undersupplied, that 'leads you to think 2028 is probably a pretty decent year as well'. He framed the constraint as easing rather than lifting - WFE grows next year while the clean-room limit 'will get somewhat better' - with the industry still 'fundamentally under-supplying demand'.
quarterly_data.figure: 2028 called 'probably a pretty decent year as well' (no number); reaffirmed: CY2026 WFE walked $135 billion -> $140 billion -> low $150 billion, 8 to 10 new tier 1 fabs through the end of 2027

quarterly_data.quarter: Lam Research Citi’s Global TMT Conference 2026 (09-09-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: HOW LAM GETS PAID ON THE PANEL TRANSITION: the growth rate itself was already on the Q4 FY2026 call - Bettinger repeated that 'Our advanced packaging business is growing north of 70% this year', with foundry and logic the big contributor. NEW is the panel readiness argument: he said the industry has not moved to the panel form factor yet but will, that it will show up in foundry and logic, and that Lam needs nothing inorganic for it because the wafer-level TSV skill set (silicon etching plus copper electroplating) carries straight over - 'we're going to be extraordinarily strong there' - helped by a company Lam acquired in Austria a few years ago that already had panel form-factor capability and 'accelerated our R&D progress there'.
quarterly_data.figure: no specific figure (advanced packaging growth north of 70% this year was already disclosed on the Q4 FY2026 call)

quarterly_data.quarter: Lam Research Citi’s Global TMT Conference 2026 (09-09-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: DRY RESIST TARGET IS GOING UP: asked to update the $1.5 billion cumulative five-year revenue opportunity Lam has previously given for Aether Dry Resist, Bettinger said 'the pull for Dry Resist is really strong. I'm quite confident that billion and a half number is going to be higher than $1.5 billion... We're going to upside that $1.5 billion', based on incremental opportunity he is hearing and seeing from customers. He is not ready to give a new number yet. He also pointed to the high-NA adoption announcements made by players in the industry over the prior day or so as 'going to be beneficial for us'.
quarterly_data.figure: $1.5 billion cumulative five-year Aether Dry Resist opportunity to be revised higher; no new number given yet

quarterly_data.quarter: Lam Research Citi’s Global TMT Conference 2026 (09-09-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: LAM'S OWN CAPACITY RESPONSE: Bettinger said Lam is pulling hard to bring a second facility in Malaysia online sooner - 'essentially a cookie cutter of the previous facility' - and is densifying existing footprints to get more output from the same square footage of clean room it already had ('you didn't know you needed to until you needed to'), plus hiring and training so Lam is 'not going to be the bottleneck'. Lam's lead time to add capacity is shorter than a customer's clean-room lead time, and the same customer demand signals (point estimate, upside, timing, error bar) are propagated back to Lam's supply chain. With thousands of parts per tool 'there's always something that is constraining us'.

quarterly_data.quarter: Lam Research Citi’s Global TMT Conference 2026 (09-09-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: WHAT IS DRIVING THE CSPG RECORD - AND THE SERVICE MODEL BEHIND IT: the headline ('third consecutive record, nearly $2.5 billion in revenue from CSPG', more than 100K installed chambers, cobots on 8 tool types) repeats the Q4/Q3 FY2026 calls. NEW is the why: Bettinger said spare parts are the biggest individual component of CSPG and 'utilization in the industry is basically at 100%, so spare parts consumption is high. That's going to continue, for sure' - the first time the utilization level itself is quantified; upgrades carry a heavy NAND footprint; and the Reliant mature-node line is strengthening in analog and industrial. He also positioned the outcome-based service model (cobots plus Equipment Intelligence and algorithmic fleet analysis) competitively for the first time - Lam is 'quite a ways ahead of this' and he expects customers to push competitors to copy it.
quarterly_data.figure: industry utilization basically at 100% driving spare-parts consumption (reaffirmed: CSPG nearly $2.5 billion, third consecutive record; cobots on 8 tool types)

quarterly_data.quarter: Lam Research Citi’s Global TMT Conference 2026 (09-09-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: NAND MODEL UPDATED BEYOND THE CALL: IR head Ram Ganesh said Lam 'recently took up the NAND SAM per wafer from 1.8x that we gave at the analyst day to 2x', because both hardware content and the complexity of the devices inflected higher than the original model assumed. The $40 billion conversion number itself is unchanged - it is a fixed amount, what it takes to go from sub 200 layers to over 200 layers - but the PACE was compressed: originally assumed over three to five years, now 'it'll be done by end of 2027'. 2026 and 2027 stay majority conversion-driven with only a little greenfield in any given year; real capacity addition is needed 'maybe like second half of 2028 and beyond', timed with fab announcements from leading customers. Bettinger added that from peak capacity to the end of this year NAND raw wafer starts are 'probably coming down 20%'. On High Bandwidth Flash: 'people are working on it. You are not seeing any volume yet', but it would combine Lam's NAND and through-silicon-via strength if it scales.
quarterly_data.figure: NAND SAM per wafer raised from 1.8x to 2x; $40 billion conversion now done by end of 2027; raw wafer starts coming down 20% from peak; greenfield capacity needed second half of 2028 and beyond
